waves.name: MAINJOB and PGMMAIN, the only job in the tree
waves.rationale: This is the only entry point, so a single wave is all the facts support. The batch-readonly family is trivially true and weak: no data edge exists, but the CALL at PGMMAIN.cbl:9 has an unbounded target, so what the job writes is unknown. The wave is deployable and rollback-able as one job (rerun the legacy JCL). Its boundary is testable only at the job return code, because neither program writes a file. It is nameable to a stakeholder only if MAINJOB is the nightly batch cycle, and the tree does not show that. Treat it as a candidate wave until the callee set is bounded.
waves.unblocks: Nothing in this tree. No other unit calls, reads from or is ordered after these two. It is a chore for sequencing purposes. Its value is that it forces the callee set of the computed CALL, and the rest of the nightly cycle, to be named.

unassigned.reason: not reached by any static edge, and 1 reachable computed call(s) could target it, for example at app/cbl/PGMMAIN.cbl:9. It moves with wave 1 if the run-time input to PGMMAIN names it.
